 Tribunal Improvement Trust, Jalandhar .....
 President & Ors.
 With
 Civil Appeal No. 9857/2025
 O R D E R

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties at length, we find no grounds made out to interfere with the impugned judgment and order dated 26.10.2016 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh in CWP No.1058 of 2014 and connected matters.

entities.text: High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Division Bench rightly noted the point of difference between the lands of the appellants when compared with the lands in the other scheme wherein additional value was given, inasmuch as the appellants lands did not directly abut National Highway-I, as was the situation in the other case.

We also find that the Land Acquisition Collector had determined the compensation payable to the appellants at 24,000/- (Rupees 19:19:07 IST twenty four thousand only) per marla, working out to 38,40,000/ (Rupees thirty-eight lakhs forty thousand only) per acre, while the High Court disagreed with the order of the reference Court and enhanced the compensation to 32,942/-
(Rupees thirty-two thousand nine hundred forty-two only) per marla, working out to 52,70,720/-
(Rupees fifty-two lakhs seventy thousand seven hundred twenty only) per acre uniformly.
Further, the High Court also extended the statutory benefits to the appellants under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The appeals are, accordingly, dismissed.
We make it clear that, in the event any part of the compensation has not been paid till date, the same shall be released within a period of two months from today.
